pipelines.overview: Brownfield pipeline definitions for extending or modifying an existing product. Use when the user wants to add features, fix bugs, refactor, or migrate (e.g. /brownfield command). Orchestrator classifies the task to select: extend | add-feature | fix-bug | refactor | migrate. When user provides JIRA ID or SOW (instead of PRD): entry is brainstorm first for extend, add-feature, and migrate — orchestrator delegates to brainstorm to deeply understand requirements with user (Q&A/brainstorm), then brainstorm hands off to architect (extend, migrate) or prd (add-feature). Fix-bug and refactor: optional brainstorm; when JIRA/SOW is a requirements input for add/enhance, use add-feature pipeline with brainstorm first. Explicit UI change: When the user explicitly requests a change in UI, use prototype (create/update) → plan (create/update) first before code; use architect (create/update) only when there is API or architecture impact — in both greenfield and brownfield. See .nayan/guidance/pipeline-entry-points.md. Product migration (legacy→new): use brownfield-migrate — architect then prototype (when UI) then plan (migration plan). For add-feature/enhance-existing-feature: when the feature is substantial or requires formal requirements or sign-off (or user provides JIRA/SOW), include brainstorm first when JIRA/SOW then prd and architect (orchestrator → brainstorm when JIRA/SOW → prd → architect → prototype/plan). When a reported "bug" is actually an enhancement (new capability, requirement change), use add-feature or extend with PRD instead of fix-bug. Brainstorm-idea is available in all pipelines so users can deep dive into the situation and explore better solution ideas before committing to a path.

pipeline.description: Product migration (legacy to new). Architect and prototype (when UI) before planning.
pipeline.when_to_use: Migrating from legacy system to new system; replacing entire product or major subsystem. When user provides JIRA ID or SOW: entry is brainstorm first to deeply understand migration scope with user, then architect. Use architect first to assess current state and plan migration architecture; then prototype (when UI) for migration UX; then plan (migration plan with sprints). Do not skip architect or prototype (when UI) — both are required before plan. Do not classify as add-feature.

pipeline.description: Add feature or enhance feature; architecture already exists.
pipeline.when_to_use: New feature or enhance existing feature within existing architecture. When user provides JIRA ID or SOW (instead of PRD): entry is brainstorm first — orchestrator → brainstorm (deep understanding with user via Q&A/brainstorm) → prd → architect (architecture impact) → prototype/plan. When user provides full PRD or feature is substantial: orchestrator → prd → architect → prototype/plan. Add/enhance with PRD always uses architect. When feature is small or spec is clear and no JIRA/SOW/PRD, skip prd: orchestrator → prototype (UI) or plan (API-only). Dev plan Section 1.1 summarizes existing; when PRD used, architect produces architecture impact per architecture-impact-add-feature.md before prototype/plan.

pipeline.description: Fix reported bug. Debug phase (diagnosis only) optional; code phase implements fix. Quality and security gates never bypassed when code changes.
pipeline.when_to_use: User reports a bug. True bug = fix incorrect behavior to match existing spec. When the "bug" is actually an enhancement (new capability, requirement change, or behavior change beyond original spec), do NOT use fix-bug: classify as brownfield-add-feature or brownfield-extend and consider PRD. When "diagnose only, then hand off fix to Code" is desired: delegate to debug (debug phase); debug hands off to code (code implementation phase). Otherwise delegate to code to diagnose and fix in one flow (systematic-debugging skill). Quality gates and security review required before deployment.
